Staff Report 
City Council 
Meeting Date: January 26, 2026 
Staff:   Niroop K. Srivatsa, City Manager
Tracy Robinson, Administrative Services Director 
Subject:   FY2025-26 Final Municipal Budget 
I N T R O D U C T I O N 
The Final Budget refines the Proposed Budget adopted by the Lafayette City Council in June and incorporates changes
approved by the City Council since then as well as recommendations from Department Directors to respond to
current conditions. 
S U M M A R Y 
The passage of the Measure H Sales Tax (1/2 cent) has given the City much needed breathing room to continue
to provide services at existing levels for at least the next six years until the tax expires. In addition to the added
revenue, the City continues to practice prudent fiscal management and restraint and therefore remains in overall
good financial health with a General Fund balance of $22.6M at the end of the fiscal year, June 30, 2025. This is equal
to 114% of annual general fund expenditures and exceeds the 60% target by $10.8M. 
However, some large projects, such as the Downtown Corridor Plan, were carried forward from the prior year, there
were savings from unfilled staff positions, and the City Council Finance Subcommittee has also recommended
substantial investments into deferred maintenance as identified in the findings of the Capital Facilities Assessment
report (see attached). Those recommendations have been incorporated into the Final Budget and as a result, the
reserve at the end of FY25-26 is projected to be $17.5M (71%) and $2.7M over the 60% target. 
The 5-Year Forecast projects that the City will be able to maintain a 60% reserve through FY29-30, however there are
small – but increasing – deficits starting in FY26-27. 
Importantly, the reduction in reserves reflected in the Final Budget is intentional and strategic. The City Council
Finance Subcommittee recommends prioritizing funding the City’s long-standing deferred maintenance needs while
reserves remain strong, and Measure H revenues are available. As a result, the Final Budget reflects a shift from
reserve accumulation toward reinvestment in critical City facilities while still maintaining the 60% threshold.
